Subject: [Helio] Dedicated GPU pool launch readiness — initial ask

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the call today — excited to get Helio onto Dedicated. Attached is the initial requirements matrix and a first-pass SOW (SOW-Redwood-Helio-v1.pdf). For our kickoff and internal handoff I need a short checklist from you so we can map responsibilities across teams. Top items we need from Helio to hit the target activation window (see proposed dates below):

- Region preference (us-east-1 / us-west-2 / eu-west-1)
- Target peak token throughput (tokens/s) and expected burst multiplier (x)
- List of IP ranges for allowlist and KMS details for key management
- Any compliance or contract redlines to route to our legal team

We plan to provision a 4-node A100 pool initially with autoscale headroom for burst to 6 nodes for 6 weeks post-launch. Proposed kickoff: Nov 3 — provisioning week Nov 8–12 — can you confirm availability for a 30-min kickoff Thurs Nov 4?

Attachments: Helio_requirements_matrix.xlsx; SOW-Redwood-Helio-v1.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary and the SOW. Quick answers inline: 

- Region: prefer us-west-2 for latency to our users in the Pacific.
- Target throughput: baseline 1,200 tokens/s, expected burst up to 2.5x during peak events (so plan for ~3,000 tokens/s burst).
- IPs: sending allowlist ranges in a separate note (you’ll get that from infra@helio.ai).
- KMS: we use a customer-managed key in AWS KMS (alias/helio/production).

We have a few redlines on the SOW around data retention and termination assistance; contracts@helio.ai will send those this afternoon. Nov 4 10:00 PT works for a 30-min kickoff.

Subject: Re: [Helio] Dedicated GPU pool launch readiness — initial ask

Sara / Karthik — looping in implementation and CS ops notes so Helio has concrete answers for provisioning and autoscale behavior. Key decisions / clarifications from our side: 

- Pool sizing: We will provision 4 x A10040GB nodes in us-west-2 initially. Steady-state capacity targets ~1,300 tokens/s; this covers your baseline and gives headroom.
- Autoscale policy: continuous scaling with target CPU/GPU utilization of 65% and predicted queue length. When queue predicts >5s median latency we scale up 1 node. Max burst policy: allow burst to +50% additional nodes for scheduled events (configurable for the first 6 weeks).
- Burst behavior: burst nodes are pre-warmed with the chosen model variant (int8 quant) for fast ramp; burst lasts up to 2 hours automatically unless extended by an operator.
- Fallbacks: If we cannot immediately satisfy burst in us-west-2 we will redirect to warm pool in us-east-1 with a model-compatible variant; we will notify via on-call and send a post-mortem for missed SLOs.

Operational links: Helio Activation Playbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CS/pages/Helio+Activation+Playbook
Kickoff workbook (editable): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-helio-kickoff

Attachments referenced: provisioning checklist (embedded in playbook) and SOW draft.

Thanks everyone — quick alignment after reviewing the redlines and the playbook: 

- Data retention: we can support a 180-day retention tier as an add-on (ops -> billable feature). I’ve asked finance to draft the addendum and will share the updated SOW by EOD tomorrow.
- Autoscale / burst: confirm policy as Marissa outlined. We will set the initial max burst to +50% nodes (operator-extensible for events).
- Activation schedule: provisioning week Nov 8–12; model validation and smoke tests Nov 15–16; go-live Nov 18 (beta traffic). Please ensure infra@helio.ai provides IP ranges and KMS key access by Nov 4 kickoff.

Next steps:
- Marissa to post a short runbook snippet into the playbook with escalation steps (done by Nov 3).
- Monica to take point on smoke test checklist and invite Helio for a live run-through Nov 15.
- Karthik to circulate updated SOW and DocuSign after legal confirms redlines.

Karthik
